title: Syed
body: Q: What are the main features of Java? Ans: Java is widely used due to its robust features that simplify development and deployment. • Object-Oriented: Everything is an object, making the code modular and reusable. • Platform Independent: Write Once, Run Anywhere (WORA) via bytecode. • Robust: Strong memory management and automatic garbage collection. • Secure: Runs inside a virtual machine (sandbox) and lacks explicit pointers.Q: What is the difference between an Abstract Class and an Interface? Ans: Both are used for abstraction, but they serve different architectural purposes. • Abstract Class: Can have both abstract (no body) and concrete (with body) methods. It supports state via instance variables. • Interface: Primarily used for defining a contract. Since Java 8, it can have default and static methods, but it cannot store state (variables are constants). • Inheritance: A class can extend only one abstract class but can implement multiple interfaces. Q: What is the 'static' keyword in Java? Ans: The static keyword is used for memory management and indicates that a member belongs to the class itself rather than an instance. • Static Variables: Shared among all instances of the class; initialized only once at the start. • Static Methods: Can be called without creating an object; they can only access other static data. • Static Block: Used to initialize static variables; it executes when the class is loaded into memory. Q: Why is the String object immutable in Java? Ans: String immutability means once a String object is created, its value cannot be changed. • String Pool: To save memory, Java reuses identical String literals. If Strings were mutable, changing one would affect all others pointing to it. • Security: Strings are used for sensitive data (usernames, passwords, URLs); immutability prevents these from being altered unexpectedly. • Thread Safety: Immutable objects are inherently thread-safe, as they cannot be modified by multiple threads simultaneously.
